protections: P1: a draft release, and anything hanging off it (its metadata and its attachments), is visible only to users with write access to the Releases unit. List and tag views already enforce this: routers/web/repo/release.go:174, routers/web/repo/release.go:285, routers/web/repo/repo.go:325, routers/api/v1/repo/release_tags.go:62-63, routers/api/v1/repo/release.go:156.

P2: an attachment is authorised against the repository it actually belongs to, not against the repository named in the URL. The repo-match check is at routers/web/repo/attachment.go:136 and the linked repo is resolved at services/repository/repository.go:238-243.

evidence: routers/web/repo/attachment.go:169 only checks perm.CanRead(unitType). The release's IsDraft is never consulted.

services/repository/repository.go:239-243 loads the release but returns only unit.TypeReleases and rel.RepoID, so the draft flag is dropped. This function is an alternative, lower-layer fix site (M3).

Three web routes reach the same sink: routers/web/web.go:820 (/attachments/{uuid}, no repo context), routers/web/web.go:1399 (/releases/attachments/{uuid}, release reader) and routers/web/web.go:1417 (legacy /{user}/{repo}/attachments/{uuid}).
routers/web/repo/repo.go:324-341 (RedirectDownload) already filters drafts by tag name before calling ServeAttachment, so the UUID routes are the open ones.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The report is about web attachment downloads. This is the API release-metadata endpoint, which needs only a release reader, and it can be read as a separate (earlier) advisory's scope.
evidence: routers/api/v1/repo/release.go:55-63 fetches the release by id and rejects only IsTag. There is no IsDraft or CanWrite check.
routers/api/v1/repo/release_tags.go:62-63 has the draft gate on the sibling by-tag endpoint, which shows the intended rule.
routers/api/v1/api.go:1319 and api.go:1335 put GET /releases/{id} under reqRepoReader(unit.TypeReleases) only.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: These endpoints return only attachment metadata. Once the web download (T1) is gated, the file bytes are protected, so a solver may judge the listing harmless.
evidence: routers/api/v1/repo/release_attachment.go:131-148 (ListReleaseAttachments) checks only RepoID, then serialises every attachment of the release.
routers/api/v1/api.go:1323 and api.go:1325 put the GETs under reqRepoReader(unit.TypeReleases) only.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The code comment says the repo-match check is deliberately skipped for legacy attachments ('The check will be ignored before this code merged'), so it reads as intended compatibility.
evidence: routers/web/repo/attachment.go:136 skips the repo-match test when attach.CreatedUnix <= LegacyAttachmentMissingRepoIDCutoff (models/repo/release.go:98, 2026-01-16).

routers/web/repo/attachment.go:165-166: when ctx.Repo.Repository is set (routes at web.go:1399 and web.go:1417), perm is the URL repo's permission. The repoID returned at attachment.go:141 from the attachment's real release or issue is ignored, so a legacy attachment can be authorised against a neighbouring repo the caller can read.

models/repo/release.go:96-97 documents that pre-cutoff rows may have repo_id=0 and must be tolerated. The natural T4 fix of dropping the cutoff and comparing attach.RepoID would 404 these attachments in their own repo. A correct fix compares against the linked repoID from attachment.go:141.

Also coupled with T1: writers must still download draft attachments (the edit page lists them at routers/web/repo/release.go:576-580). The uploader-only rule for unlinked attachments (attachment.go:147-151) and reader access to published-release attachments must keep working.

masking: T3 hands out attachment UUIDs and browser_download_url values for draft releases. Until T1 is fixed those URLs download the file. After T1, T3's residual leak is metadata only, which is what makes T3 easy to dismiss.

conflicts.what: Enforcing the repo match by removing the cutoff at attachment.go:136 (attach.RepoID != ctx.Repo.Repository.ID) breaks legacy attachments with repo_id=0 in their own repo (models/repo/release.go:96-97). The fix must use the linked repoID from GetAttachmentLinkedTypeAndRepoID.

Gating release attachments on CanWrite(TypeReleases) unconditionally (instead of only for drafts) breaks reader downloads of published release assets via ServeAttachment and RedirectDownload (routers/web/repo/repo.go:333-341).

fairness_risks: Readers must keep downloading attachments of published releases, including through /releases/download/latest/{file} (routers/web/repo/repo.go:344-359).
Writers must keep fetching draft attachments (draft edit page, routers/web/repo/release.go:576-580), and an attachment's uploader must keep access to it while it is unlinked (attachment.go:147-151).

TagsList deliberately includes drafts for code readers (routers/web/repo/release.go:217-219, with a comment saying this is intended). A hidden test must not treat this as a leak, or it contradicts documented behaviour.
Legacy attachments (created before the cutoff, repo_id=0) must still be served in their own repository.

design.why: There are four independent fix sites, each with a different reason to dismiss. T1 is the advisory route the report points at. T2 is an API sibling that can be dismissed as another advisory's scope (deepseek type). T3 can be dismissed as metadata only once T1 is fixed (deepseek type, with masking). T4 can be dismissed by an explicit code comment framing it as legacy compatibility (deepseek xhard). The coupled legacy repo_id=0 value (T5, same group as T4) supplies the mimo-type pressure, since an over-hardening fix for T4 breaks legacy attachments, and T1 adds the 'do not gate published assets' coupling. Dropping T3 leaves a 3-trap design that is still valid but has less spread.
